tools.name: windows_list
tools.title: List windows
tools.description: List the document windows open in MarkdownPoint as { windows }: each one’s root path, null for a window with no presentation, and which is focused. A tool that acts on a presentation takes one of these roots as "root". Omit it to use the focused one, or the only one open when none is focused. presentations_open, presentations_create, capabilities and schema need no open presentation.

tools.name: presentations_open
tools.title: Open a presentation
tools.description: Show an existing presentation folder in a MarkdownPoint document window, or focus the window that already shows it. Needs no open presentation. Returns the canonical root to pass as "root" to the other tools.

root.description: Absolute folder of an existing presentation.
The canonical root the app now shows.

opened.description: False when a window already showed it and was focused instead.

tools.name: presentations_create
tools.title: Create a presentation
tools.description: Create a presentation folder from a bundled theme (Basic when omitted) and show it in a document window. Needs no open presentation. Each bundled theme starts the presentation with one slide. Returns the canonical root to pass as "root" to the other tools.

root.description: Absolute folder to create; its parent must exist and the folder must not.

theme.description: A bundled theme's name or key; the default theme when omitted.

tools.name: presentations_close
tools.title: Close a presentation

root.description: Absolute folder of a presentation a window shows.
The root whose windows closed, once each had saved.

tools.name: capabilities
tools.title: Read the contract
tools.description: Contract version, served methods, accepted operation names and limits: the app's, whichever presentation is open, or none. Read exact request fields with schema.

app.description: The app that answers: its version, as `mdpoint --version` and MCP's server info give it.

methods.description: What the app serves itself, with no presentation, and what it serves for one.

operations.description: Operation types `proposals.create` takes; `schema` serves each one's exact request contract.

interpolations.description: The named interpolations; a key may instead carry four cubic-bezier numbers [x1, y1, x2, y2] with x within 0–1.

outputSchema.description: The app's contract, the same whichever presentation is open, or none.

envelopeBytes.description: An envelope travels as one line, one string, so it is at most the longest string, counted in bytes: an ASCII envelope's characters.

longestEdge.description: The longest edge a rendered slide or frame can have: the longest side any export writes.

proposalOperations.description: Operations one proposal carries: it is applied as one kernel batch.

heldProposals.description: Proposals waiting at once: each stays in memory until it is accepted or rejected.

rangeSamples.description: Samples one `slides.frames` or `slides.measure` request takes: each renders the slide, and a frame's PNG is held until the answer is sent.

traceSamples.description: Samples one `slides.trace` request reads: each samples the whole animation once, and a frame rate times a range could reach billions.

tools.name: schema
tools.title: Read a request’s schema
tools.description: Read the request schema for one operation, exports.run or themes.edit, with only its referenced definitions. Use it before proposals_create for each operation you send, and themes.edit before themes_edit. Omit selector for the complete proposal schema. With detail: "fields", it lists the request’s fields in place of its schema: each one’s type, whether every request needs it, its values when the schema names them, and its description. Without a selector, it lists the proposal request’s own fields, then each operation’s name and the fields it always needs. This only reads the contract; it never proposes or edits. It needs no open presentation.

selector.description: One operation's name, exports.run or themes.edit; omitted, the complete proposal request.

detail.description: `fields` answers with an index of the request's fields in place of its schema.

tools.name: presentations_get
tools.title: Read the presentation
tools.description: Current diagnostics, revision, slide IDs, the presentation’s own properties as updatePresentationProperties sets them (footer, date, locale, default transition, soundtrack, self-playing) the slides and sections in order (outline), and the accepted theme catalog: layout keys and their placeholders, schemes and text styles. Use those keys when inserting or changing slides. Each issue has a severity: error or warning. Its disposition says what the app does about it: fallback, skip-object, refuse-slide or refuse-document. Warnings with code text-overflow name each object whose words run past its frame on a slide as its builds leave it, where they still show (slides_render’s fits give the frame that holds them); text-hidden names each object some of whose words the slide’s edge, the end of their path or their table cell hides, which an export asks about; and text-overflow-unchecked says that could not be measured. It reads the files first: when they cannot be taken in, as after a hand edit the parser refuses, `stalled` gives the reason and the parser errors, and the rest describes the presentation as last read.

root.description: Presentation root path to target (from windows_list). Omit to use the focused window, or the only open presentation when none is focused.

stalled.description: Present while the presentation cannot take in its files, as after a hand edit the parser refuses: `revision` and `issues` still describe the presentation as last read, and this says why the files on disk are not it, with the parser's errors about them.

tools.description: Render one slide through the app renderer at authored Base or an exact animation position. Base is the authored composition; Start applies initial values. tools.name: slides_measure
tools.title: Measure a slide’s 3D content
tools.description: Measure a step’s 3D content over a range of its time, or with rests: true the slide at every rest its show makes, from the geometry the page poses. For each model and 3D text at each time: its bounds on the slide and its shadows’, how much of each text’s box its silhouette and its shadow cover, and how far its lowest point stands above the slide’s floor, its highest floor object. A model covers flat words where its silhouette falls on their box through the camera, whichever of them draws in front, and 3D words only where it draws in front of their letters. A shadow covers a text where it falls on its box. A shadow here is the sharp outline its parts cast on each catcher. A render shows what is seen. Over the range: for a model with an in-place walk, how fast its planted feet slide against its body’s travel, and the speed each walk travels at its size, at which its feet hold; and for each text, the most it is covered and shadowed, and when. Numbers decide what a picture misjudges: a model landing beside words, feet sliding, a shadow over a headline. With rests: true in place of stepId and a range: the slide at every rest its show makes, where it holds until the next click. That is as it has appeared when its first click waits, after each click once that click’s steps, their with and after members, its Actions and the camera’s drift have ended, and after the last. A rest that loops is measured over one period, fps times a second, 30 when omitted: its 3D’s loop, or its 2D’s while the 3D stands still; where both loop at lengths of their own, the 2D on its own clock over the 3D’s period. A rest where the show holds the 3D still while something in it would move on gives its hold, the cause and the objects to change, as the slide’s warning does: fix it, or the show freezes the 3D there. Each sample adds how much of each object draws, 0 to 1, its opacity and its groups’, 0 while hidden; and for each text, the most a drawn model covers it while it draws, and at which rest. At most 120 samples. Nothing changes.

tools.name: models_build
tools.title: Build a 3D model
tools.description: Build a 3D model from code and save it as media/<name>-<hash>.glb, a file a model object can show. source is an ES module whose default export build(kit, data) returns { model, actions }: a three.js Object3D in glTF meters, +Y up, facing +Z, its origin where it stands (a character’s feet), and its AnimationClips. kit holds THREE, GLTFExporter, GLTFLoader, SVGLoader, FontLoader, TextGeometry, ConvexGeometry, ParametricGeometry, RoundedBoxGeometry, BufferGeometryUtils, SkeletonUtils, SimplifyModifier, TessellateModifier and MeshSurfaceSampler; model(file), which loads a model of the presentation named in models; and separate(mesh), which makes each piece no edge joins an object of its own beside it, its origin at its bounds center, for an Action to turn or move. A material named color:<role> takes the slide’s color of that role. userData { markdownpoint: { "cast-shadow": false } } on an object, or { markdownpoint: { loop: true } } on an AnimationClip, which becomes an Action, become its extras. It runs in a sandbox with no network or files, for at most 60 s. The model is imported as a file is: lights and cameras removed, Actions named apart. The source runs only while it builds. No file keeps it. To change a model you built, build it again from new source. Returns the file, changes, the report models_inspect gives, and a sheet: the saved model from eight sides, top and side, and each Action at four times. To make a text object’s words 3D, give for: { slideId, objectId }: data.words then holds its letters as its slide lays them out, which kit.text(data.words, { depth, bevel }) extrudes into { model, letters }, one node per letter, one model unit an em of the text’s size, the origin on its first baseline at the left of its column. Without source, the app’s letter builder makes them at data’s depth and bevel, in ems (0.2 and 0.02 when left out). The model’s file keeps those and for, saved as generated/<name>-<hash>.glb: a text’s model is MarkdownPoint’s, not one of the author’s media. The answer adds built-from: set the text’s model to { file: the answer’s file, "built-from": its built-from } with updateObjectProperties, and the slide draws the model while the words are the ones built; once the words or font change, it draws them flat until you build it again.

tools.name: proposals_create

tools.description: If operation fields appear as unknown, call schema with the operation name. Propose a change against a fresh revision from presentations_get or slides_get. The app tries the operations, each with exactly the keys the schema gives it, without writing them; nothing is written until proposals_accept. Use stable slide/object/step ids from slides_get; it also discovers parameter targets, current values and interpolation. Initial values, timed keys and cues use the shared agent contract. New key/cue ids must be fresh within a step; reusing an id replaces its whole record. A null key value clears an optional property to its text-style/default, while a null updateStep entry deletes that key or cue. insertSlide takes an optional slideId of your choosing and objects to seed the new slide. insertObject takes an optional objectId. It can’t name a slide inserted by the same proposal. A proposal its validation refuses is not held: the call fails with validation-failed, and the error's validation holds its errors and warnings; an error with code no-change means everything is already so. Otherwise read the proposal's warnings and summaries, then accept it by its id as one undo step.
